work.name: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (in collaboration with Amazon Music)
work.position: M.S.(R) Thesis Researcher — Modelling Popularity Bias in Recommender Systems
work.summary: Advised by Prof. Arpit Agarwal. Currently under review at AAAI 27 (arXiv:2608.10474).
highlights: Formulated a theoretical framework using differential equations modelling popularity bias in recommender systems.
Derived and proved concrete theorems using stochastic approximation to predict and quantify user drop-off.
Designed a mitigation solution using equalized odds to prevent popularity bias without loss in system accuracy.
Evaluated the framework using 410 million real-world interactions, validating theoretical predictions and the mitigation solution.

work.name: Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.
work.summary: Technologies: AWS SageMaker, AWS S3, DataBricks, NVIDIA CUDA
highlights: Identified recommendation system biases causing 5% of 20,000 catalogue items to absorb 84.5% of interactions.
Developed two Inverse Propensity Scoring (IPS) models to ensure fairness and integrated them using a 35% signal blend across 7,016 users.
Achieved a 60% reduction in top 10% popularity concentration, effectively cutting the NDCG@6 cost by half.
Developed a dynamic visualisation dashboard using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to track model performance.

Coordinated cross-functional team updates by resolving JIRA requests, ensuring sprint timelines were followed.
Maintained task work orders via internal Wiki pages, enabling strict compliance tracking for project leads.

projects.name: Inducing Robustness in 2D-DPO
projects.summary: Course: CS 769 | Guide: Prof. Ganesh Ramakrishnan
highlights: Diagnosed a lack of segment-level noise robustness in 2D-DPO, causing a win-rate drop from 43% to 37%.
Formulated Robust 2D-DPO and trained a Pythia 6.9B model on 6,400 HelpSteer-2D prompts to test robustness.
Attained a win-rate rise from 37% to 45% in the presence of noise, indicating robustness towards noisy labels.
Accelerated model training and inference by parallelising over 4 NVIDIA H100 GPUs.

projects.name: RLHF under User Heterogeneity
projects.summary: Course: CS 6103 | Guide: Prof. Arpit Agarwal
highlights: Uncovered a flaw in standard RLHF due to the assumption of perfectly homogeneous preferences across all users.
Engineered personalised preference models across 40 workers and 2 distinct clusters using vector embeddings.
Achieved 53% and 52.7% win-rates, outperforming the baseline 52% win-rate across both user clusters.

projects.name: OCR-based MCQ Solver
projects.summary: Course: GNR 638 | Guide: Prof. Biplab Bannerjee
highlights: Procured and scraped high-quality MCQ questions on Deep Learning topics to train an OCR solver.
Trained an 8-billion-parameter Qwen3-VL model to perform OCR extraction and solve MCQ questions.
Attained 90% accuracy using few-shot training when graded against a pre-defined evaluation dataset.

projects.name: Improved ResNet Implementation (iResNet-50)
projects.summary: Course: GNR 638 | Guide: Prof. Biplab Bannerjee
highlights: Addressed information flow obstruction, lossy projection, and sub-optimal normalisation in deep ResNet-50.
Implemented the iResNet-50 model from scratch and trained for 100 epochs to overcome ResNet-50 bottlenecks.
Achieved 85.31% Top-1 accuracy using a 25.56M parameter iResNet-50 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

projects.name: Fine-tuning & Evaluating CNN Backbones
projects.summary: Course: GNR 638 | Guide: Prof. Biplab Bannerjee
highlights: Benchmarked three pre-trained CNN architectures across the Aerial Image Dataset (AID) with 30 classes.
Executed 5 evaluation paradigms highlighting few-shot performance and noise robustness across the models.
Observed 95% accuracy and a 24% relative drop due to noise for ConvNeXt-Tiny (27.8M parameters).

projects.name: Microchess Playing Agent
projects.summary: Course: CS 747 | Guide: Prof. Shivaram Kalyankrishnan
highlights: Devised a Microchess agent using reinforcement learning to compete against random and rational opponents.
Engineered Negamax algorithm with Alpha-Beta pruning and Quiescence search for modelling gameplay.
Achieved 94% and 84% win-rates against random and rational opponents respectively across 100 games.

projects.name: Blackjack Bot
projects.summary: Course: CS 747 | Guide: Prof. Shivaram Kalyankrishnan
highlights: Modelled a 26-card Blackjack variation as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) with three specific actions.
Implemented Linear Programming and Howard's Policy Iteration to solve linear constraints across scenarios.
Evaluated optimal value functions against agent actions and passed 100% of defined test cases.

projects.name: Emotion Classification for Hindi
projects.summary: Course: CS 626 | Guide: Prof. Pushpak Bhattacharya
highlights: Classified 20,000 Hindi sentences into five distinct emotion classes using deep learning models.
Verified 162 scenarios spanning 9 deep learning models across 6 dataset variations and 3 word-embedding techniques.
Attained 84.3% accuracy using TextBlob embeddings and mBERT with human-annotated labels.

projects.name: Machine Learning over Encrypted Data
highlights: Identified 250 million medical data breaches and the need for encryption when handling sensitive medical records.
Developed a Python framework using Homomorphic Encryption, enabling operations directly on encrypted data.
Performed linear and logistic regression accurately on encrypted data without decryption.
